submission.justification: Crystal-K3 gives clearly the best energy resolution at 662 keV. Simulated FWHM (100k events): K3 2.71–3.32% for 3–8 cm (5 cm: 3.02%; 4 cm: 2.88%; 6 cm: 2.71% and 2.91% in two runs). K1 at 5 cm: 4.35%. K2 at 5 cm: 8.71%. These results agree with the 2025 summary (2.9 / 4.5 / 8.5%). For K3, results from 4 to 6 cm differ by less than the run-to-run spread (about ±0.2%). So I picked 5 cm, the nominal and well-studied thickness in the middle of that flat range. Results get slightly worse at 7–8 cm. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: none of the project documents give data on the crystals' own radioactivity (intrinsic radioactivity) or radiopurity. That is the deciding factor for 'suitable for low-background operation'. Shielding (lead, copper, radon purge) does not reduce radioactivity inside the crystal. Some high-light-yield, fast inorganic scintillators (e.g. lanthanum-halide types) carry significant intrinsic activity, which would rule them out for material screening. Before any Q2 procurement, measure or get vendor data on the radioactivity of K3, K1 and K2 (K/Th/U chains and any intrinsic isotopes). If K3 fails, the next choice for resolution is K1 (about 4.3–4.9%).

requirements.requirement: Best possible energy resolution at 662 keV
requirements.evidence: K3 at 5 cm: 3.02% FWHM, and K3 is about 2.7–3.0% from 4 to 6 cm. K1 at 5 cm: 4.35%. K2 at 5 cm: 8.71%. Matches the 2025 simulation summary.
